transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Gupta (Redwood CSM); Ethan Blake (Lucid Core CTO), Priya Shah (Head of Data), Samir Patel (SRE)

Summary:
Quick QBR to review past quarter usage, cost spikes in May, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is evaluating a private deployment pilot to reduce egress costs and meet latency SLOs. Agreed to run benchmarks and share security artifacts.

[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining for the QBR, um we'll keep to 45 minutes. quick agenda — usage & costs, reliability review, roadmap items and next steps.
[00:15] Ethan Blake: thanks Alicia. yeah i wanted to focus on the may spike — we saw token usage jump and cost went up, we need to understand where that came from.
[00:30] Maya Gupta: quick context, we pulled the route-level cost sheet, looks like two routes had higher tail requests; we'll share the sheet after the call.
[00:45] Priya Shah: for us the spike correlated with a marketing push and heavier multi-turn chat sessions; memory / kv cache wasn't warming as expected.
[01:05] Jamal Ortiz: that aligns — we saw cold-kv cache hits and some token re-generation, also a couple long prompt chains. we recommended prefix caching and adaptive batching changes earlier.
[01:25] Samir Patel: question, if we enable more aggressive batching won't p95 latency increase? our SLAs are strict for session storefront.
[01:40] Jamal Ortiz: good question — batching policy is workload aware, you can set max latency SLOs per route; we can keep p95 under target while benefiting from batching for throughput. we'll propose concrete config.
[02:05] Ethan Blake: also curious about dedicated vs hosted — is dedicated enough to address egress/cost concerns or do we need private on-prem?
[02:20] Alicia Park: dedicated reduces per-token cost with reserved capacity and predictable throughput; private (VPC/on-prem) helps with data residency and egress — depends on whether egress charges from cloud providers are the main driver.
[02:40] Priya Shah: egress is material. plus we have compliance reviews next quarter — SOC2 documentation and audit logs are mandatory.
[02:55] Maya Gupta: we will share SOC2 report and audit-log configs. Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and we can show RBAC settings in the console.
[03:15] Ethan Blake: can you send me the security whitepaper link now?
[03:20] Maya Gupta: yes I'll send in the follow-up along with the QBR deck.
[03:35] Priya Shah: reliability: we had two incidents in April and May, one was a model deployment that increased latency, another was a routing fallback. can you summarize?
[03:50] Jamal Ortiz: incident 1 — model rollout led to higher token generation time due to sequence length mismatch; we mitigated by pinning previous model and rolling back. incident 2 — routing fallback triggered when a capacity zone was saturated; we have auto-fallback policies but the fallback route had slightly different latency profile. both fixed; postmortems shared.
[04:20] Samir Patel: were the postmortems attached to the incident page? we didn't get the full timeline.
[04:35] Maya Gupta: we'll re-share the incident timeline and the remediation steps.
[04:50] Ethan Blake: ok on costs — can you show the predicted savings if we adopt quantized model variants and enable prefix caching? numbers would help the CFO.
[05:05] Jamal Ortiz: with int8 quantization and KV prefix caching we estimate 20-35% per-token cost reduction depending on request mix; we'll run a tailored calc and include in the deck.
[05:30] Priya Shah: what about quality regressions with quantization? we've seen hallucinations increase elsewhere.
[05:45] Jamal Ortiz: valid concern — Redwood Optimize runs evals tied to prompt sets; we can run A/B with your representative prompts to measure quality delta and only promote profiles that meet your thresholds.
[06:10] Alicia Park: roadmap notes — upcoming features: improved batching controls (Q3), longer-context kernel selection improvements (Q4), and deeper RBAC audit logs (imminent).
[06:30] Ethan Blake: timeline for longer-context kernels? we have some multi-turn legal docs that go long.
[06:40] Jamal Ortiz: longer-context improvements slated for late Q4; we can discuss temporary workarounds (segmentation + context window stitching) in the technical follow-up.
[07:00] Priya Shah: on private deployment — what's the onboarding timeline and what support is needed from our infra?
[07:15] Alicia Park: private deployments typically 6-10 weeks depending on cluster readiness and network setup; we'll need network engineers for VPC peering, KMS access, and pull the benchmarks.
[07:30] Samir Patel: do you support on-prem air-gapped options?
[07:35] Jamal Ortiz: yes, there's an on-prem package for air-gapped environments; it'll need a support SLA and we provide an ops runbook.
[07:50] Ethan Blake: great. let's schedule the benchmark. Maya, can you coordinate with Jamal?
[08:00] Maya Gupta: yes I'll set up the session and invite the infra folks.
[08:10] Priya Shah: for the benchmark we will provide sample traffic and p95 target; when do you need that data?
[08:20] Jamal Ortiz: asap ideally by 6/18 so we can configure the runner.
[08:35] Alicia Park: recap — we'll send the deck, security docs, and a cost-savings calc. Jamal will run the benchmark. Priya will share traffic patterns. next check-in to review results.
[08:55] Ethan Blake: last question — competitors were mentioned in our RFP; how does Redwood compare specifically on observability and per-route cost reporting?
[09:10] Alicia Park: we offer token-level cost breakdowns, route dashboards, and per-model latency histograms; we emphasize production telemetry with trace hooks you can ingest. we'll share a sample dashboard.
[09:30] Priya Shah: please include exportable CSVs for our FP&A team.
[09:35] Maya Gupta: will do.
[09:50] Samir Patel: one small thing, can we see retention settings for logs? compliance needs 12 months retention.
[10:00] Maya Gupta: yes we can configure retention and offer long-term storage add-on.
[10:10] Alicia Park: ok wrapping — action items as discussed. thanks everyone.

Referenced artifacts:
- QBR deck (to be shared)
- Route-level cost CSV (link to be sent)
- SOC2 report and security whitepaper (will share)
- Benchmark harness / results (to be scheduled)

End of transcript.
